title: The service desk is an identity control, and attackers know it
angle: Sits squarely where IT support and security meet. The helpdesk password reset is a real attack path, and the fix is a workflow change rather than a product.
keyPoints: Helpdesks are a frequent social engineering target because they sit where identity, access and urgent requests meet.
Remote and hybrid work made it worse: agents are less likely to personally know the person calling, so impersonation is easier.
Deepfake helpdesk calls and AI assisted social engineering are part of the current threat picture, not a hypothetical one.

A concrete control: require verification such as a live video call, photo ID or manager attestation before issuing a Temporary Access Pass, and make that pass one time use with a short validity window.
Pair it with a standing script that refuses out of band reset requests where the ticket origin has not been verified.
On the authentication side, FIDO2 and WebAuthn passkeys tie approval to a device or cryptographic key, which is what actually defeats push bombing, SIM swapping and credential phishing.

sources.title: Anatomy of a Helpdesk Social Engineering Attack
